note: Election of three town commissioners in the Town Hall on Wednesday 15 January 1902. The outgoing members, Michael Smyth, J.P., Dr. Dorman and John Nugent (chairman), sought re-election, with John Hughes as a fourth candidate. Peter M'Knight, town clerk, returning officer; John Conroy, poll clerk. Nugent received 53 plumpers. The Irish News gives the same figures (its 185 for Smyth is faintly printed). No party labels are printed. Michael Smyth: no party label printed in 1902. At other elections he stood as Nationalist (Keady, Armagh County Council, 6 April 1899, printed 'N': Lurgan Mail, 15 April 1899, p. 6 ("Election Results: Armagh Co. Council Returns"); party labels from the Northern Star, 15 April 1899, p. 5, and the Portadown News, 15 April 1899, p. 8; figures checked against those two and the Portadown News, 8 April 1899, p. 5; Keady, Armagh County Council, 28 May 1902, printed 'N.': Banbridge Chronicle, 31 May 1902, p. 3 ("Local Government Elections": Armagh County Council); nominations and labels also in the Armagh Guardian, 2 May 1902, p. 2 ("But Few Contests": county council nominations, with labels); Keady, Armagh County Council, 25 May 1905, printed 'N': Armagh Guardian, 2 June 1905, p. 5 ("Council Elections: 2 Unionist Gains, 1 Nationalist"); candidates in the Armagh Guardian, 28 April 1905, p. 5 ("Nominations: County Councillors")). John Nugent: no party label printed in 1902. At other elections he stood as Nationalist (Keady, Armagh County Council, 6 April 1899, printed 'N': Lurgan Mail, 15 April 1899, p. 6 ("Election Results: Armagh Co. Council Returns"); party labels from the Northern Star, 15 April 1899, p. 5, and the Portadown News, 15 April 1899, p. 8; figures checked against those two and the Portadown News, 8 April 1899, p. 5; Keady Rural, Armagh Rural District, 28 May 1902, printed 'N.': Northern Whig, 30 May 1902, p. 8 (Armagh rural district results); nominations from the Armagh Guardian, 2 May 1902, p. 2 ("District Councils": nominations with labels, withdrawals, and "Newry"); Keady, Armagh County Council, 28 May 1902, printed 'N.': Banbridge Chronicle, 31 May 1902, p. 3 ("Local Government Elections": Armagh County Council); nominations and labels also in the Armagh Guardian, 2 May 1902, p. 2 ("But Few Contests": county council nominations, with labels)).
